page.locator('[data-testid=\"recovery-textarea\"]');\n  await textarea.fill(mnemonic);\n\n  // Click --recover\n  const submitBtn = page.locator('[data-testid=\"recovery-submit\"]');\n  await submitBtn.click();\n\n  // Wait for recovery to complete (redirects to /files)\n  await page.waitForURL('**/files', { timeout });\n}\n\n/**\n * Wait for the DeviceApprovalModal to appear on an existing device.\n *\n * This modal shows when a new device requests approval and the existing\n * device is polling for pending requests.\n *\n * @param page - Page of the existing (approver) device\n * @param options.timeout - Max time to wait (default: 60s)\n */\nexport async function waitForDeviceApproval(\n  page: Page,\n  options: { timeout?: number } = {}\n): Promise<void> {\n  const timeout = options.timeout ?? 60_000;\n  await page.locator('[data-testid=\"device-approval-modal\"]').waitFor({\n    state: 'visible',\n    timeout,\n  });\n}\n\n/**\n * Click the --approve button on the DeviceApprovalModal.\n *\n * Assumes the modal is already visible (use waitForDeviceApproval first).\n */\nexport async function approveDevice(page: Page): Promise<void> {\n  const approveBtn = page.locator('[data-testid=\"device-approval-approve\"]');\n  await approveBtn.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 5_000 });\n  await approveBtn.click();\n  // Wait for modal to dismiss after approval completes\n  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=\"device-approval-modal\"]')).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });\n}\n\n/**\n * Click the --deny button on the DeviceApprovalModal.\n *\n * Assumes the modal is already visible (use waitForDeviceApproval first).\n */\nexport async function denyDevice(page: Page): Promise<void> {\n  const denyBtn = page.locator('[data-testid=\"device-approval-deny\"]');\n  await denyBtn.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 5_000 });\n  await denyBtn.click();\n  // Wait for modal to dismiss after deny completes\n  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=\"device-approval-modal\"]')).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });\n}\n"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/tests/e2e/tests/mfa-flows.spec.ts",
  "content": "import { test, expect, type Page, type BrowserContext } from '@playwright/test';\nimport {\n  setupMockWallet,\n  createWalletContext,\n  loginViaWallet,\n} from '../utils/wallet-login-helpers';\nimport {\n  navigateToSecurityTab,\n  getMfaStatusText,\n  enrollMfa,\n  enterRecoveryPhrase,\n  waitForDeviceApproval,\n  approveDevice,\n  denyDevice,\n} from '../utils/mfa-helpers';\n\n/**\n * MFA E2E Flow Tests (TC-MFA-01 through TC-MFA-05)\n *\n * Tests the full MFA lifecycle using real wallet login (Core Kit\n * initialization via @johanneskares/wallet-mock). Serial execution\n * is required because MFA enrollment in TC-MFA-01 persists for\n * subsequent tests.\n *\n * Architecture:\n * - Primary browser context acts as the \"existing device\" throughout.\n * - New contexts are created for \"new device\" scenarios (TC-MFA-03/04/05).\n * - All contexts use the same Hardhat account #0 wallet address, so\n *   Core Kit maps them to the same DKG identity.\n *\n * Network:\n * - Core Kit operations hit Web3Auth Sapphire Devnet (5-15s per op).\n * - Full suite may take 60-120s.\n * - Tagged @mfa for optional CI filtering.\n *\n * Prerequisites:\n * - Local API running at http://localhost:3000\n * - Local web app running at http://localhost:5173\n * - Fresh backend DB (each run creates a unique userId for the wallet address)\n */\ntest.describe.serial('MFA flows @mfa', () => {\n  let primaryContext: BrowserContext;\n  let primaryPage: Page;\n  let recoveryPhrase: string;\n\n  test.beforeAll(async ({ browser }) => {\n    // Create primary context with mock wallet\n    primaryContext = await browser.newContext();\n    primaryPage = await primaryContext.newPage();\n    await setupMockWallet(primaryPage);\n  });\n\n  test.afterAll(async () => {\n    await primaryContext.close();\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-01: Wallet login and MFA enrollment\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-01: wallet login and MFA enrollment', async () => {\n    test.setTimeout(120_000); // Core Kit init + enableMFA can be slow\n\n    // 1. Login via wallet (happy path — no MFA yet)\n    const result = await loginViaWallet(primaryPage, { timeout: 60_000 });\n    expect(result.outcome).toBe('success');\n\n    // 2. Navigate to Settings → Security tab\n    await navigateToSecurityTab(primaryPage);\n\n    // 3. Verify MFA is currently disabled\n    const statusBefore = await getMfaStatusText(primaryPage);\n    expect(statusBefore).toBe('[DISABLED]');\n\n    // 4. Run through the enrollment wizard\n    //    This calls enableMFA on Devnet (~10-15s), generates recovery phrase,\n    //    requires acknowledge checkbox, and confirms success.\n    recoveryPhrase = await enrollMfa(primaryPage, { enableTimeout: 60_000 });\n\n    // 5. Verify we got a valid 24-word phrase\n    const words = recoveryPhrase.split(' ');\n    expect(words).toHaveLength(24);\n    expect(words.every((w) => w.length > 0)).toBe(true);\n\n    // 6. Verify MFA is now enabled in the Security tab\n    const statusAfter = await getMfaStatusText(primaryPage);\n    expect(statusAfter).toBe('[ENABLED]');\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-02: MFA status reflected in Security tab\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-02: MFA status reflected in Security tab', async () => {\n    test.setTimeout(30_000);\n\n    // Navigate to Security tab (same context as enrollment)\n    await navigateToSecurityTab(primaryPage);\n\n    // Status badge should show [ENABLED]\n    const status = await getMfaStatusText(primaryPage);\n    expect(status).toBe('[ENABLED]');\n\n    // Factor info should be visible with factor count\n    const factorInfo = primaryPage.locator('.security-tab-factor-info');\n    await expect(factorInfo).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });\n    const factorText = await factorInfo.textContent();\n    expect(factorText).toMatch(/\\d+ factors active/);\n\n    // The --enable-mfa button should NOT be visible (MFA already enabled)\n    await expect(primaryPage.locator('[data-testid=\"mfa-enable-btn\"]')).not.toBeVisible();\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-03: Device approval — approve\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-03: device approval - approve', async ({ browser }) => {\n    test.setTimeout(120_000);\n\n    // 1. Ensure primary page is on /files (approver device, polls for requests)\n    await primaryPage.evaluate(() => {\n      window.location.hash = '#/files';\n    });\n    await primaryPage.waitForURL('**/files', { timeout: 15_000 });\n\n    // 2. Create new context B (no localStorage = new device)\n    const { context: contextB, page: pageB } = await createWalletContext(browser);\n\n    try {\n      // 3. Login via wallet on context B → should enter REQUIRED_SHARE\n      const resultB = await loginViaWallet(pageB, { timeout: 60_000 });\n      expect(resultB.outcome).toBe('requiredShare');\n\n      // 4. Wait for DeviceWaitingScreen on context B\n      await expect(pageB.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting\"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });\n\n      // 5. Wait for DeviceApprovalModal on primary page\n      //    (polling picks up the approval request from context B)\n      await waitForDeviceApproval(primaryPage, { timeout: 60_000 });\n\n      // 6. Approve the request on primary page\n      await approveDevice(primaryPage);\n\n      // 7. Wait for context B to complete login → redirect to /files\n      await pageB.waitForURL('**/files', { timeout: 60_000 });\n    } finally {\n      await contextB.close();\n    }\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-04: Recovery phrase restore\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-04: recovery phrase restore', async ({ browser }) => {\n    test.setTimeout(120_000);\n\n    // 1. Create new context C (new device)\n    const { context: contextC, page: pageC } = await createWalletContext(browser);\n\n    try {\n      // 2. Login via wallet → should enter REQUIRED_SHARE\n      const resultC = await loginViaWallet(pageC, { timeout: 60_000 });\n      expect(resultC.outcome).toBe('requiredShare');\n\n      // 3. Wait for DeviceWaitingScreen\n      await expect(pageC.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting\"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });\n\n      // 4. Click \"use recovery phrase instead\"\n      const recoveryLink = pageC.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting-recovery-link\"]');\n      await recoveryLink.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 10_000 });\n      await recoveryLink.click();\n\n      // 5. Enter recovery phrase and submit\n      await enterRecoveryPhrase(pageC, recoveryPhrase, { timeout: 60_000 });\n\n      // 6. Verify page redirected to /files (recovery succeeded)\n      await expect(pageC).toHaveURL(/.*files/);\n    } finally {\n      await contextC.close();\n    }\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-05: Device approval — deny\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-05: device approval - deny', async ({ browser }) => {\n    test.setTimeout(120_000);\n\n    // 1. Ensure primary page is on /files (denier device)\n    await primaryPage.evaluate(() => {\n      window.location.hash = '#/files';\n    });\n    await primaryPage.waitForURL('**/files', { timeout: 15_000 });\n\n    // 2. Create new context D (new device)\n    const { context: contextD, page: pageD } = await createWalletContext(browser);\n\n    try {\n      // 3. Login via wallet → should enter REQUIRED_SHARE\n      const resultD = await loginViaWallet(pageD, { timeout: 60_000 });\n      expect(resultD.outcome).toBe('requiredShare');\n\n      // 4. Wait for DeviceWaitingScreen on context D\n      await expect(pageD.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting\"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });\n\n      // 5. Wait for DeviceApprovalModal on primary page\n      await waitForDeviceApproval(primaryPage, { timeout: 60_000 });\n\n      // 6. Deny the request on primary page\n      await denyDevice(primaryPage);\n\n      // 7. Verify context D shows \"Request was denied\" message\n      const statusMessage = pageD.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting-status\"]');\n      await expect(statusMessage).toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });\n      const statusText = await statusMessage.textContent();\n      expect(statusText).toContain('denied');\n    } finally {\n      await contextD.close();\n    }\n  });\n});\n"
}

Everything looks correct. Here's a summary of all changes:

## Changes Made

### 1. `data-testid` attributes added to 6 MFA components

| Component | Test IDs Added |
|-----------|---------------|
| **MfaEnrollmentWizard.tsx** | `mfa-wizard`, `mfa-wizard-step-1/2/3`, `mfa-wizard-continue`, `mfa-wizard-cancel`, `mfa-wizard-back`, `mfa-wizard-done`, `mfa-wizard-loading`, `mfa-wizard-error`, `mfa-wizard-acknowledge` |
| **RecoveryPhraseGrid.tsx** | `recovery-phrase-grid` |
| **DeviceWaitingScreen.tsx** | `device-waiting`, `device-waiting-status` (on denied/expired/error), `device-waiting-countdown`, `device-waiting-retry`, `device-waiting-recovery-link` |
| **RecoveryInput.tsx** | `recovery-input`, `recovery-textarea`, `recovery-submit`, `recovery-back`, `recovery-error` |
| **DeviceApprovalModal.tsx** | `device-approval-modal`, `device-approval-approve`, `device-approval-deny`, `device-approval-device-name` |
| **SecurityTab.tsx** | `security-tab`, `mfa-status-badge`, `mfa-enable-btn` |

### 2. New E2E helper: `tests/e2e/utils/wallet-login-helpers.ts`
- `setupMockWallet(page)` — installs EIP-6963 mock wallet before navigation
- `createWalletContext(browser)` — creates an isolated context with mock wallet
- `loginViaWallet(page)` — drives the full wallet → SIWE → Core Kit flow, returns `success` or `requiredShare`

### 3. New E2E helper: `tests/e2e/utils/mfa-helpers.ts`
- `navigateToSecurityTab(page)` — navigate to Settings → Security tab
- `getMfaStatusText(page)` — read `[ENABLED]`/`[DISABLED]` badge
- `enrollMfa(page)` — full wizard flow, returns 24-word recovery phrase
- `extractRecoveryPhrase(page)` — read words from grid
- `enterRecoveryPhrase(page, mnemonic)` — fill and submit recovery form
- `waitForDeviceApproval(page)` — wait for approval modal
- `approveDevice(page)` / `denyDevice(page)` — respond to approval request

### 4. New E2E test suite: `tests/e2e/tests/mfa-flows.spec.ts`
- **TC-MFA-01**: Wallet login → MFA enrollment → capture recovery phrase
- **TC-MFA-02**: Security tab reflects MFA enabled state
- **TC-MFA-03**: New device → approval from existing device
- **TC-MFA-04**: New device → recovery phrase restore
- **TC-MFA-05**: New device → deny approval → denied status shown

### Verification
- Web app build passes (`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build`)
- E2E TypeScript compiles cleanly (`tsc --noEmit`)

## Summary: `enableMfa` Hook and Core Kit Provider Analysis

Based on my thorough code analysis, here's what happens during MFA enablement and what could cause auth state changes or navigation:

### 1. **`useMfa` Hook - `enableMfa` Function**
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/hooks/useMfa.ts` (lines 66-119)

The `enableMfa` function performs these critical steps:

```typescript
const enableMfa = useCallback(async (): Promise<string> => {
  if (!coreKit) throw new Error('Core Kit not initialized');
  if (coreKit.status !== COREKIT_STATUS.LOGGED_IN) {
    throw new Error('Must be logged in to enable MFA');
  }

  const store = useMfaStore.getState();
  if (store.isMfaEnabled) {
    throw new Error('MFA is already enabled');
  }

  useMfaStore.getState().setEnrolling(true);  // Set enrolling state
  try {
    // 1. CRITICAL: commitChanges() MUST be called first (manualSync mode)
    await coreKit.commitChanges();

    // 2. Capture TSS public key BEFORE enableMFA for stability verification
    const preMfaTssPub = coreKit.getKeyDetails().tssPubKey;

    // 3. enableMFA creates device factor + recovery factor atomically
    const backupFactorKeyHex = await coreKit.enableMFA({
      shareDescription: FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.SeedPhrase,
    });

    // 4. Commit the MFA changes
    await coreKit.commitChanges();

    // 5. Defensive check: verify TSS public key unchanged after MFA enrollment
    const postMfaTssPub = coreKit.getKeyDetails().tssPubKey;
    if (preMfaTssPub?.x && preMfaTssPub?.y && postMfaTssPub?.x && postMfaTssPub?.y) {
      const preX = preMfaTssPub.x.toString('hex');
      const preY = preMfaTssPub.y.toString('hex');
      const postX = postMfaTssPub.x.toString('hex');
      const postY = postMfaTssPub.y.toString('hex');
      if (preX !== postX || preY !== postY) {
        throw new Error(
          'MFA enrollment failed: TSS public key changed. Your keypair identity is no longer stable. Please contact support.'
        );
      }
    }

    // 6. Convert to 24-word mnemonic for user display
    const mnemonic = keyToMnemonic(backupFactorKeyHex);

    // 7. Update store with new key details
    const details = coreKit.getKeyDetails();
    useMfaStore.getState().setMfaEnabled(true);  // Update MFA enabled state
    useMfaStore.getState().setFactorDetails(details.totalFactors, details.threshold);

    return mnemonic;
  } finally {
    useMfaStore.getState().setEnrolling(false);  // Clear enrolling state
  }
}, [coreKit]);
```

**Key Points:**
- Does NOT call `syncStatus()` to change the Core Kit React context status
- Does NOT navigate away
- Only modifies the **MFA store** state (local to the MFA module)
- Returns the 24-word mnemonic string for the UI to display

### 2. **Core Kit Provider - `enableMFA` Method**
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/core-kit-provider.tsx`

The Core Kit provider itself provides:
- `coreKit`: The singleton Core Kit instance
- `status`: Current COREKIT_STATUS 
- `syncStatus()`: Function to sync React context with Core Kit's internal status

**`enableMFA()` is a method on the Core Kit instance itself** (from `@web3auth/mpc-core-kit` library), not on the provider. It:
- Creates a device factor for the current device
- Creates a recovery factor (seed phrase)
- Atomically increases TSS threshold from 2 to 3

### 3. **MFA Store**
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/stores/mfa.store.ts`

```typescript
type MfaState = {
  isMfaEnabled: boolean;      // Whether MFA is active
  isEnrolling: boolean;        // True during enableMFA() call
  factorCount: number;         // Total factors from getKeyDetails()
  threshold: number;           // Threshold from getKeyDetails()
  hasSeenPrompt: boolean;      // Session dismissal flag
  
  setMfaEnabled: (enabled: boolean) => void;
  setEnrolling: (enrolling: boolean) => void;
  setFactorDetails: (count: number, threshold: number) => void;
  dismissPrompt: () => void;
  reset: () => void;
};
```

### 4. **MFA Enrollment Wizard - Where Navigation/Auth Changes Occur**
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/components/mfa/MfaEnrollmentWizard.tsx` (lines 29-51)

The wizard calls `enableMfa()` and handles the **completion callback**:

```typescript
const handleEnableMfa = useCallback(async () => {
  setIsLoading(true);
  setError(null);
  try {
    const phrase = await enableMfa();        // Call the hook
    setMnemonic(phrase.split(' '));
    setIsLoading(false);
  } catch (err) {
    setIsLoading(false);
    // Check if MFA was partially enabled (server succeeded but post-check failed)
    const mfaStatus = checkMfaStatus();
    if (mfaStatus.isMfaEnabled) {
      setPartiallyEnabled(true);
      setError(
        'MFA was enabled but an error occurred. Please close this dialog and use ' +
          '"Regenerate Recovery Phrase" in Settings > Security to obtain your recovery phrase.'
      );
    } else {
      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to enable MFA');
    }
  }
}, [enableMfa, checkMfaStatus]);
```

**On Step 3 completion**, the wizard calls:
```typescript
const handleGoToStep3 = useCallback(() => {
  setMnemonic([]);
  setStep(3);
}, []);

// Then in the UI (line 250):
onClick={onComplete}  // Calls the onComplete prop
```

### 5. **Security Tab - The Parent Component**
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/components/mfa/SecurityTab.tsx` (lines 30-33)

```typescript
const handleEnrollmentComplete = useCallback(() => {
  setShowWizard(false);           // Close the wizard dialog
  checkMfaStatus();               // Verify MFA was enabled
}, [checkMfaStatus]);
```

**Then passes to the wizard:**
```tsx
<MfaEnrollmentWizard
  onComplete={handleEnrollmentComplete}
  onCancel={handleEnrollmentCancel}
/>
```

### 6. **Auth State & useAuth Hook**
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts`

The `useAuth` hook is **NOT called during MFA enablement**. It handles:
- Login flows (Google, Email, Wallet)
- Logout
- Session restoration
- Backend auth token management
- Navigation to `/files`

MFA enablement **does NOT trigger**:
- ❌ `syncStatus()` in the Core Kit context
- ❌ Navigation to `/files` or any route
- ❌ Changes to auth state (access token, isAuthenticated)
- ❌ Vault initialization or key loading
- ❌ Device registry sync

It **only updates**:
- ✅ MFA store state (`isMfaEnabled`, `isEnrolling`, `factorCount`, `threshold`)
- ✅ Local UI state in the Security Tab component

### 7. **Critical Design Rule**
**From useMfa.ts comments (lines 122-132):**

```typescript
/**
 * Input a factor key (hex string) to complete REQUIRED_SHARE login.
 * Used for both recovery and cross-device approval flows.
 *
 * IMPORTANT: Does NOT call syncStatus() because doing so would transition
 * Core Kit's React context to LOGGED_IN, which triggers the session
 * restoration effect in useAuth.ts. Since backend auth hasn't completed yet
 * (no valid access token or refresh cookie), the session restore fails and
 * calls coreKitLogout(), effectively undoing the recovery.
 *
 * The caller (completeRequiredShare) is responsible for syncing status
 * AFTER backend auth completes.
 */
```

This principle applies to `enableMFA()` as well — it deliberately avoids calling `syncStatus()` to prevent unintended auth state changes.

> AGENT

Now it's clear: `loginViaWallet` returned `requiredShare` because MFA is already enabled for the Hardhat account #0 identity on Sapphire Devnet from a previous test run. The local DB persists the same userId between runs.

The fix: use a **random private key** for each test run instead of the well-known Hardhat key. This gives a unique wallet address → unique userId → fresh DKG identity on Devnet → no pre-existing MFA state.

  "content": "import { test, expect, type Page, type BrowserContext } from '@playwright/test';\nimport type { PrivateKeyAccount } from 'viem/accounts';\nimport {\n  createTestAccount,\n  setupMockWallet,\n  createWalletContext,\n  loginViaWallet,\n} from '../utils/wallet-login-helpers';\nimport {\n  navigateToSecurityTab,\n  getMfaStatusText,\n  enrollMfa,\n  enterRecoveryPhrase,\n  waitForDeviceApproval,\n  approveDevice,\n  denyDevice,\n} from '../utils/mfa-helpers';\n\n/**\n * MFA E2E Flow Tests (TC-MFA-01 through TC-MFA-05)\n *\n * Tests the full MFA lifecycle using real wallet login (Core Kit\n * initialization via @johanneskares/wallet-mock). Serial execution\n * is required because MFA enrollment in TC-MFA-01 persists for\n * subsequent tests.\n *\n * Architecture:\n * - A random private key is generated per test run, giving a unique\n *   wallet address -> unique backend userId -> fresh DKG identity on\n *   Sapphire Devnet. This ensures no pre-existing MFA state.\n * - Primary browser context acts as the \"existing device\" throughout.\n * - New contexts are created for \"new device\" scenarios (TC-MFA-03/04/05).\n * - All contexts use the same random account so Core Kit maps them to\n *   the same DKG identity.\n *\n * Network:\n * - Core Kit operations hit Web3Auth Sapphire Devnet (5-15s per op).\n * - Full suite may take 60-120s.\n * - Tagged @mfa for optional CI filtering.\n *\n * Prerequisites:\n * - Local API running at http://localhost:3000\n * - Local web app running at http://localhost:5173\n */\ntest.describe.serial('MFA flows @mfa', () => {\n  let account: PrivateKeyAccount;\n  let primaryContext: BrowserContext;\n  let primaryPage: Page;\n  let recoveryPhrase: string;\n\n  test.beforeAll(async ({ browser }) => {\n    // Generate a random wallet identity for this test run\n    account = createTestAccount();\n\n    // Create primary context with mock wallet\n    primaryContext = await browser.newContext();\n    primaryPage = await primaryContext.newPage();\n    await setupMockWallet(primaryPage, account);\n  });\n\n  test.afterAll(async () => {\n    await primaryContext.close();\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-01: Wallet login and MFA enrollment\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-01: wallet login and MFA enrollment', async () => {\n    test.setTimeout(120_000); // Core Kit init + enableMFA can be slow\n\n    // 1. Login via wallet (happy path — no MFA yet, fresh identity)\n    const result = await loginViaWallet(primaryPage, { timeout: 60_000 });\n    expect(result.outcome).toBe('success');\n\n    // 2. Navigate to Settings → Security tab\n    await navigateToSecurityTab(primaryPage);\n\n    // 3. Verify MFA is currently disabled\n    const statusBefore = await getMfaStatusText(primaryPage);\n    expect(statusBefore).toBe('[DISABLED]');\n\n    // 4. Run through the enrollment wizard\n    //    This calls enableMFA on Devnet (~10-15s), generates recovery phrase,\n    //    requires acknowledge checkbox, and confirms success.\n    recoveryPhrase = await enrollMfa(primaryPage, { enableTimeout: 60_000 });\n\n    // 5. Verify we got a valid 24-word phrase\n    const words = recoveryPhrase.split(' ');\n    expect(words).toHaveLength(24);\n    expect(words.every((w) => w.length > 0)).toBe(true);\n\n    // 6. Verify MFA is now enabled in the Security tab\n    const statusAfter = await getMfaStatusText(primaryPage);\n    expect(statusAfter).toBe('[ENABLED]');\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-02: MFA status reflected in Security tab\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-02: MFA status reflected in Security tab', async () => {\n    test.setTimeout(30_000);\n\n    // Navigate to Security tab (same context as enrollment)\n    await navigateToSecurityTab(primaryPage);\n\n    // Status badge should show [ENABLED]\n    const status = await getMfaStatusText(primaryPage);\n    expect(status).toBe('[ENABLED]');\n\n    // Factor info should be visible with factor count\n    const factorInfo = primaryPage.locator('.security-tab-factor-info');\n    await expect(factorInfo).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });\n    const factorText = await factorInfo.textContent();\n    expect(factorText).toMatch(/\\d+ factors active/);\n\n    // The --enable-mfa button should NOT be visible (MFA already enabled)\n    await expect(primaryPage.locator('[data-testid=\"mfa-enable-btn\"]')).not.toBeVisible();\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-03: Device approval — approve\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-03: device approval - approve', async ({ browser }) => {\n    test.setTimeout(120_000);\n\n    // 1. Ensure primary page is on /files (approver device, polls for requests)\n    await primaryPage.evaluate(() => {\n      window.location.hash = '#/files';\n    });\n    await primaryPage.waitForURL('**/files', { timeout: 15_000 });\n\n    // 2. Create new context B (no localStorage = new device, same wallet identity)\n    const { context: contextB, page: pageB } = await createWalletContext(browser, account);\n\n    try {\n      // 3. Login via wallet on context B → should enter REQUIRED_SHARE\n      const resultB = await loginViaWallet(pageB, { timeout: 60_000 });\n      expect(resultB.outcome).toBe('requiredShare');\n\n      // 4. Wait for DeviceWaitingScreen on context B\n      await expect(pageB.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting\"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });\n\n      // 5. Wait for DeviceApprovalModal on primary page\n      //    (polling picks up the approval request from context B)\n      await waitForDeviceApproval(primaryPage, { timeout: 60_000 });\n\n      // 6. Approve the request on primary page\n      await approveDevice(primaryPage);\n\n      // 7. Wait for context B to complete login → redirect to /files\n      await pageB.waitForURL('**/files', { timeout: 60_000 });\n    } finally {\n      await contextB.close();\n    }\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-04: Recovery phrase restore\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-04: recovery phrase restore', async ({ browser }) => {\n    test.setTimeout(120_000);\n\n    // 1. Create new context C (new device, same wallet identity)\n    const { context: contextC, page: pageC } = await createWalletContext(browser, account);\n\n    try {\n      // 2. Login via wallet → should enter REQUIRED_SHARE\n      const resultC = await loginViaWallet(pageC, { timeout: 60_000 });\n      expect(resultC.outcome).toBe('requiredShare');\n\n      // 3. Wait for DeviceWaitingScreen\n      await expect(pageC.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting\"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });\n\n      // 4. Click \"use recovery phrase instead\"\n      const recoveryLink = pageC.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting-recovery-link\"]');\n      await recoveryLink.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 10_000 });\n      await recoveryLink.click();\n\n      // 5. Enter recovery phrase and submit\n      await enterRecoveryPhrase(pageC, recoveryPhrase, { timeout: 60_000 });\n\n      // 6. Verify page redirected to /files (recovery succeeded)\n      await expect(pageC).toHaveURL(/.*files/);\n    } finally {\n      await contextC.close();\n    }\n  });\n\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  // TC-MFA-05: Device approval — deny\n  // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  test('TC-MFA-05: device approval - deny', async ({ browser }) => {\n    test.setTimeout(120_000);\n\n    // 1. Ensure primary page is on /files (denier device)\n    await primaryPage.evaluate(() => {\n      window.location.hash = '#/files';\n    });\n    await primaryPage.waitForURL('**/files', { timeout: 15_000 });\n\n    // 2. Create new context D (new device, same wallet identity)\n    const { context: contextD, page: pageD } = await createWalletContext(browser, account);\n\n    try {\n      // 3. Login via wallet → should enter REQUIRED_SHARE\n      const resultD = await loginViaWallet(pageD, { timeout: 60_000 });\n      expect(resultD.outcome).toBe('requiredShare');\n\n      // 4. Wait for DeviceWaitingScreen on context D\n      await expect(pageD.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting\"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });\n\n      // 5. Wait for DeviceApprovalModal on primary page\n      await waitForDeviceApproval(primaryPage, { timeout: 60_000 });\n\n      // 6. Deny the request on primary page\n      await denyDevice(primaryPage);\n\n      // 7. Verify context D shows \"Request was denied\" message\n      const statusMessage = pageD.locator('[data-testid=\"device-waiting-status\"]');\n      await expect(statusMessage).toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });\n      const statusText = await statusMessage.textContent();\n      expect(statusText).toContain('denied');\n    } finally {\n      await contextD.close();\n    }\n  });\n});\n"
}

Perfect! Now I have a complete understanding. Let me compile my findings.

## Investigation Complete

Based on my thorough code analysis, here's what I found regarding the MFA enrollment navigation issue:

### **Root Cause: No Status Change Events During enableMFA/commitChanges**

The @web3auth/mpc-core-kit SDK **does not emit status change events** during `commitChanges()` or `enableMFA()`. The Core Kit provider relies on **manual status synchronization** via the `syncStatus()` function.

### **Key Code Sections:**

#### 1. **Core Kit Provider** (`apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/core-kit-provider.tsx`)

```typescript
// Line 64-67: syncStatus is MANUAL only
const syncStatus = useCallback(() => {
  const ck = getCoreKit();
  setStatus(ck.status);
}, []);

// Lines 42, 66: React state only updates when setStatus() is called explicitly
const [status, setStatus] = useState<COREKIT_STATUS>(COREKIT_STATUS.NOT_INITIALIZED);
```

**Problem:** The status is only updated when `syncStatus()` is explicitly called. There's no polling, no event listeners, and no automatic status change detection.

#### 2. **Authentication Derivation** (`apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts`)

```typescript
// Lines 41-50: isAuthenticated comes from authStore, NOT CoreKit status
const {
  accessToken,
  isAuthenticated,  // <- This is the key
  lastAuthMethod,
  userEmail,
  setAccessToken,
  // ...
} = useAuthStore();

// Line 66: isLoading includes coreKitInitialized
const isLoading = !coreKitInitialized || isLoggingIn || isLoggingOut;
```

```typescript
// apps/web/src/stores/auth.store.ts, line 49:
// isAuthenticated is set ONLY when accessToken is set
setAccessToken: (token) => set({ accessToken: token, isAuthenticated: true }),
```

#### 3. **SettingsPage Redirect** (`apps/web/src/routes/SettingsPage.tsx`, lines 67-71)

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isLoading && !isAuthenticated) {
    navigate('/');
  }
}, [isAuthenticated, isLoading, navigate]);
```

**Critical Discovery:** If `isAuthenticated` becomes false while on the settings page, this effect triggers a redirect to `/`.

#### 4. **MFA Enrollment** (`apps/web/src/hooks/useMfa.ts`, lines 66-119)

```typescript
const enableMfa = useCallback(async (): Promise<string> => {
  // Line 80: commitChanges BEFORE enableMFA
  await coreKit.commitChanges();

  // Line 86: enableMFA creates device + recovery factors
  const backupFactorKeyHex = await coreKit.enableMFA({
    shareDescription: FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.SeedPhrase,
  });

  // Line 91: commitChanges AFTER enableMFA
  await coreKit.commitChanges();
  
  // NO syncStatus() call here!
  // ...
}, [coreKit]);
```

**Key Issue:** `enableMfa()` does NOT call `syncStatus()` after `commitChanges()`. The React component's status remains stale.

### **The Vulnerability Chain:**

1. ✅ User is on `/settings` with `isAuthenticated = true`
2. ✅ User clicks "Enable MFA" → `enableMfa()` is called
3. ✅ `commitChanges()` completes silently (no status change emitted by SDK)
4. ⚠️ **No `syncStatus()` is called** — React state is NOT updated
5. ⚠️ If any other code path briefly clears the accessToken or updates auth state, `isAuthenticated` becomes false
6. ❌ The `useEffect` in SettingsPage sees `!isAuthenticated && !isLoading`
7. ❌ Navigation to `/` is triggered, interrupting the MFA wizard

### **Why This Is Insidious:**

- The SDK doesn't provide event callbacks for status changes during `commitChanges()` or `enableMFA()`
- React state and Web3Auth internal state can diverge silently
- The SettingsPage guard effect is **synchronous** and fires immediately if auth state changes
- There's no debounce or confirmation that auth is truly lost

### **Missing Integration Points:**

1. **No status polling** - The provider should optionally poll `coreKit.status` periodically
2. **No event subscription** - The SDK doesn't emit events, and the provider doesn't listen for them
3. **No explicit sync in enableMfa()** - After `commitChanges()`, the hook should call `syncStatus()`
4. **No transient auth state** - There's no way to mark auth as "in-progress during MFA" vs. "lost"

---

## **Relevant File Paths:**

- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/core-kit-provider.tsx` - No automatic status detection
- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/core-kit.ts` - Singleton wrapper, no listeners
- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/hooks.ts` - `doLoginWithCoreKit()` has `syncStatus()` but it's not used everywhere
- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/hooks/useMfa.ts` - `enableMfa()` missing `syncStatus()` call
- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts` - Auth state decoupled from Core Kit status
- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/routes/SettingsPage.tsx` - Redirect guard that can fire mid-MFA
- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/stores/auth.store.ts` - `isAuthenticated` is accessToken-based only

The fix requires ensuring `syncStatus()` is called (or auth state is protected) during MFA operations.

> AGENT

Found it! Line 62 of `client.ts`: when an API request gets a 401 and the token refresh also fails, `useAuthStore.getState().logout()` is called — setting `isAuthenticated = false`. During the long `enableMFA()` Devnet operation, a background API call (sync polling, etc.) could 401, and if the refresh fails, the app logs out and SettingsPage redirects.

This is a real bug the E2E test exposed. The fix: SettingsPage should not redirect during MFA enrollment (use the `isEnrolling` flag from the MFA store).

     1→import axios from 'axios';
     2→import { useAuthStore } from '../../stores/auth.store';
     3→import { useVaultStore } from '../../stores/vault.store';

     5→import { useSyncStore } from '../../stores/sync.store';
     6→
     7→// Shared refresh promise eliminates race condition where multiple concurrent
     8→// 401 responses each trigger their own POST /auth/refresh before the boolean
     9→// flag could be set. The promise is assigned synchronously before any await,
    10→// so all concurrent 401 handlers see it immediately and share the same refresh.
    11→let refreshPromise: Promise<string> | null = null;
    12→
    13→export const apiClient = axios.create({
    14→  baseURL: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || 'http://localhost:3000',
    15→  withCredentials: true, // For HTTP-only refresh token cookie
    16→});
    17→
    18→// Request interceptor: Add access token to headers
    19→apiClient.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
    20→  const accessToken = useAuthStore.getState().accessToken;
    21→  if (accessToken) {
    22→    config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
    23→  }
    24→  return config;
    25→});
    26→
    27→// Response interceptor: Handle 401 and token refresh
    28→apiClient.interceptors.response.use(
    29→  (response) => response,
    30→  async (error) => {
    31→    const originalRequest = error.config;
    32→
    33→    // Don't retry refresh endpoint to avoid infinite loop
    34→    const isRefreshRequest = originalRequest?.url?.includes('/auth/refresh');
    35→
    36→    // Only handle 401 errors, and only retry once (but never retry refresh endpoint)
    37→    if (error.response?.status === 401 && !originalRequest._retry && !isRefreshRequest) {
    38→      originalRequest._retry = true;
    39→
    40→      // If a refresh is already in flight, all concurrent 401 handlers
    41→      // await the same promise instead of firing duplicate refresh requests.
    42→      if (refreshPromise) {
    43→        const token = await refreshPromise;
    44→        originalRequest.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
    45→        return apiClient(originalRequest);
    46→      }
    47→
    48→      // First 401 handler: create the refresh promise synchronously (before any await)
    49→      // so subsequent 401 handlers in the same microtask see it immediately.
    50→      refreshPromise = apiClient
    51→        .post<{ accessToken: string }>('/auth/refresh')
    52→        .then((response) => {
    53→          const { accessToken } = response.data;
    54→          useAuthStore.getState().setAccessToken(accessToken);
    55→          return accessToken;
    56→        })
    57→        .catch((refreshError) => {
    58→          // [SECURITY: HIGH-03] Clear all stores including crypto keys on token refresh failure
    59→          useFolderStore.getState().clearFolders();
    60→          useVaultStore.getState().clearVaultKeys();
    61→          useSyncStore.getState().reset();
    62→          useAuthStore.getState().logout();
    63→          // Redirect to login will be handled by route guard
    64→          throw refreshError;
    65→        })
    66→        .finally(() => {
    67→          refreshPromise = null;
    68→        });
    69→
    70→      const token = await refreshPromise;
    71→      originalRequest.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
    72→      return apiClient(originalRequest);
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    throw error;
    76→  }
    77→);

     5→type MfaEnrollmentWizardProps = {

    10→type WizardStep = 1 | 2 | 3;
    11→
    12→/**
    13→ * Step-by-step MFA enrollment wizard.
    14→ *
    15→ * Step 1: Explain what MFA does and that it cannot be undone.
    16→ * Step 2: Enable MFA, display recovery phrase, require acknowledgment.
    17→ * Step 3: Confirmation that MFA is enabled with factor count.
    18→ */
    19→export function MfaEnrollmentWizard({ onComplete, onCancel }: MfaEnrollmentWizardProps) {
    20→  const { enableMfa, checkMfaStatus, factorCount, threshold } = useMfa();
    21→
    22→  const [step, setStep] = useState<WizardStep>(1);
    23→  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);
    24→  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
    25→  const [mnemonic, setMnemonic] = useState<string[]>([]);
    26→  const [partiallyEnabled, setPartiallyEnabled] = useState(false);
    27→  const [acknowledged, setAcknowledged] = useState(false);
    28→
    29→  const handleEnableMfa = useCallback(async () => {
    30→    setIsLoading(true);
    31→    setError(null);
    32→    try {
    33→      const phrase = await enableMfa();
    34→      setMnemonic(phrase.split(' '));
    35→      setIsLoading(false);
    36→    } catch (err) {
    37→      setIsLoading(false);
    38→      // If MFA was partially enabled (server succeeded but post-check failed),
    39→      // guide user to recovery instead of a broken retry loop
    40→      const mfaStatus = checkMfaStatus();
    41→      if (mfaStatus.isMfaEnabled) {
    42→        setPartiallyEnabled(true);
    43→        setError(
    44→          'MFA was enabled but an error occurred. Please close this dialog and use ' +
    45→            '"Regenerate Recovery Phrase" in Settings > Security to obtain your recovery phrase.'
    46→        );
    47→      } else {
    48→        setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to enable MFA');
    49→      }
    50→    }
    51→  }, [enableMfa, checkMfaStatus]);
    52→
    53→  const handleGoToStep2 = useCallback(() => {
    54→    setStep(2);
    55→    if (mnemonic.length === 0) {
    56→      handleEnableMfa();
    57→    }

    70→

    96→          <div className={`mfa-wizard-progress-segment ${step >= 3 ? 'complete' : ''}`} />

    10→import { getCoreKit, initCoreKit, COREKIT_STATUS } from './core-kit';
    11→import type { Web3AuthMPCCoreKit } from './core-kit';
    12→
    13→interface CoreKitContextValue {
    14→  /** The Core Kit singleton instance (null until first render) */
    15→  coreKit: Web3AuthMPCCoreKit | null;
    16→  /** Current SDK status from the COREKIT_STATUS state machine */
    17→  status: COREKIT_STATUS;
    18→  /** True when status is anything other than NOT_INITIALIZED */
    19→  isInitialized: boolean;
    20→  /** True when status is LOGGED_IN (user fully authenticated) */
    21→  isLoggedIn: boolean;
    22→  /** True when status is REQUIRED_SHARE (MFA challenge needed -- Phase 12.4) */
    23→  isRequiredShare: boolean;
    24→  /** Initialization error, if any */
    25→  error: Error | null;
    26→  /** Re-run initialization (e.g., retry after error) */
    27→  reinitialize: () => Promise<void>;
    28→  /** Sync React state with CoreKit's internal status after login/logout/MFA */
    29→  syncStatus: () => void;
    30→}
    31→
    32→const CoreKitContext = createContext<CoreKitContextValue | null>(null);
    33→
    34→/**
    35→ * React context provider for MPC Core Kit.
    36→ *
    37→ * Initializes Core Kit on mount (calls init() which checks for existing sessions).
    38→ * Exposes the singleton instance and COREKIT_STATUS to child components.
    39→ * Mounted at the top of the component tree in main.tsx.
    40→ */
    41→export function CoreKitProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
    42→  const [status, setStatus] = useState<COREKIT_STATUS>(COREKIT_STATUS.NOT_INITIALIZED);
    43→  const [coreKit, setCoreKit] = useState<Web3AuthMPCCoreKit | null>(null);
    44→  const [error, setError] = useState<Error | null>(null);
    45→
    46→  const initialize = useCallback(async () => {
    47→    try {
    48→      setError(null);
    49→      const ck = getCoreKit();
    50→      setCoreKit(ck);
    51→      const resultStatus = await initCoreKit();
    52→      setStatus(resultStatus);
    53→    } catch (err) {
    54→      console.error('[CoreKit] Initialization failed:', err);
    55→      setError(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)));
    56→    }
    57→  }, []);
    58→
    59→  useEffect(() => {
    60→    initialize();
    61→  }, [initialize]);
    62→
    63→  /** Sync React state with CoreKit's internal status. Call after login/logout/MFA. */
    64→  const syncStatus = useCallback(() => {
    65→    const ck = getCoreKit();
    66→    setStatus(ck.status);
    67→  }, []);
    68→
    69→  const value: CoreKitContextValue = useMemo(
    70→    () => ({
    71→      coreKit,
    72→      status,
    73→      isInitialized: status !== COREKIT_STATUS.NOT_INITIALIZED,
    74→      isLoggedIn: status === COREKIT_STATUS.LOGGED_IN,
    75→      isRequiredShare: status === COREKIT_STATUS.REQUIRED_SHARE,
    76→      error,
    77→      reinitialize: initialize,
    78→      syncStatus,
    79→    }),
    80→    [coreKit, status, error, initialize, syncStatus]
    81→  );
    82→
    83→  return <CoreKitContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CoreKitContext.Provider>;
    84→}
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * Hook to access Core Kit instance and status from React components.
    88→ * Must be used within a CoreKitProvider.
    89→ */
    90→export function useCoreKit(): CoreKitContextValue {
    91→  const context = useContext(CoreKitContext);
    92→  if (!context) {
    93→    throw new Error('useCoreKit must be used within CoreKitProvider');
    94→  }
    95→  return context;
    96→}

OK, the Core Kit provider only updates its status via explicit `syncStatus()` calls, not automatically during `enableMFA()`. That rules out Core Kit status changes as the trigger.

Given the user's crucial observation that manual testing works fine, this is almost certainly a **timing/race condition specific to E2E**. The most likely scenario: a late-firing `navigate('/files')` from the login flow fires after the test has already navigated to `/settings`.

> AGENT

Now I have the root cause. The stack trace shows:

```
useAuth.ts:247 → Login.tsx:87 → WalletLoginButton.tsx:58 (handleSiweFlow)
```

The Login component has a redirect effect that fires `navigate('/files')` whenever `isAuthenticated` is true. During the login flow, there are TWO sources of `navigate('/files')`:
1. `loginWithWallet` calls it directly after `completeBackendAuth`
2. Login's `useEffect(() => { if (isAuthenticated) navigate('/files') }, [isAuthenticated, navigate])` fires when `isAuthenticated` changes

In E2E, the test catches the first navigate, immediately moves to `/settings`, but the second navigate fires in the next React render cycle and redirects back to `/files`.

The fix: make Login's redirect effect only fire when the user is actually on the login page:

> TOOL

> AGENT

Found it. The Login component's redirect effect at line 53-57 fires `navigate('/files')` whenever `isAuthenticated` changes. During the login flow, this fires twice — once immediately, and once more on a subsequent re-render caused by `setIsLoggingIn(false)`, which happens after the test has already navigated away.

The fix: check that we're still on the login page before redirecting:

> TOOL

   123→export async function extractRecoveryPhrase(page: Page): Promise<string> {

   132→    if (text) words.push(text.trim());

   135→  if (words.length !== 24) {

     1→import { type BrowserContext, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
     2→import { installMockWallet } from '@johanneskares/wallet-mock';
     3→import { generatePrivateKey, privateKeyToAccount, type PrivateKeyAccount } from 'viem/accounts';
     4→import { mainnet } from 'viem/chains';
     5→import { http } from 'viem';
     6→
     7→/**
     8→ * Result of a wallet login attempt.
     9→ * - `success`: Login completed, page redirected to /files.
    10→ * - `requiredShare`: MFA is enabled and this device needs an additional share
    11→ *   (DeviceWaitingScreen is shown).
    12→ */
    13→export type WalletLoginResult =
    14→  | { outcome: 'success' }
    15→  | { outcome: 'requiredShare' };
    16→
    17→/**
    18→ * Generate a random viem account for MFA tests.
    19→ *
    20→ * Each test run uses a unique private key → unique wallet address →
    21→ * unique userId in the backend → fresh DKG identity on Sapphire Devnet.
    22→ * This ensures no pre-existing MFA state from previous runs.
    23→ *
    24→ * The account should be shared across all tests in a serial suite so
    25→ * that the same Core Kit identity is used throughout.
    26→ */
    27→export function createTestAccount(): PrivateKeyAccount {
    28→  return privateKeyToAccount(generatePrivateKey());
    29→}
    30→
    31→/**
    32→ * Set up a mock wallet on a page (must be called BEFORE navigation).
    33→ *
    34→ * Creates an EIP-6963 mock provider that auto-announces itself.
    35→ * wagmi's injected() connector auto-discovers it.
    36→ *
    37→ * @param page - Playwright page
    38→ * @param account - viem account to use for signing (all contexts must share the same account)
    39→ */
    40→export async function setupMockWallet(page: Page, account: PrivateKeyAccount): Promise<void> {
    41→  await installMockWallet({
    42→    page,
    43→    account,
    44→    defaultChain: mainnet,
    45→    transports: { [mainnet.id]: http() },
    46→  });
    47→}
    48→
    49→/**
    50→ * Create a new browser context with a mock wallet installed.
    51→ *
    52→ * Returns the context and its first page, both with the mock wallet
    53→ * ready. The context must be closed by the caller.
    54→ *
    55→ * @param browser - Playwright browser instance
    56→ * @param account - viem account to use (same account across all contexts)
    57→ */
    58→export async function createWalletContext(
    59→  browser: { newContext: () => Promise<BrowserContext> },
    60→  account: PrivateKeyAccount
    61→): Promise<{ context: BrowserContext; page: Page }> {
    62→  const context = await browser.newContext();
    63→  const page = await context.newPage();
    64→  await setupMockWallet(page, account);
    65→  return { context, page };
    66→}
    67→
    68→/**
    69→ * Perform a full wallet login via the UI.
    70→ *
    71→ * Drives the real wallet -> SIWE -> Core Kit flow:
    72→ * 1. Navigate to login page
    73→ * 2. Wait for Core Kit init (wallet button becomes enabled)
    74→ * 3. Click [WALLET] button -> connector list appears
    75→ * 4. Select "Mock Wallet" connector
    76→ * 5. Wait for either:
    77→ *    - /files redirect (success, no MFA or device already known)
    78→ *    - DeviceWaitingScreen (MFA enabled, new device needs share)
    79→ *
    80→ * The mock wallet auto-approves connect + signMessage, so the SIWE
    81→ * flow proceeds without user interaction.
    82→ *
    83→ * @param page - Page with mock wallet already installed via setupMockWallet()
    84→ * @param options.timeout - Max time to wait for login outcome (default: 60s)
    85→ */
    86→export async function loginViaWallet(
    87→  page: Page,
    88→  options: { timeout?: number } = {}
    89→): Promise<WalletLoginResult> {
    90→  const timeout = options.timeout ?? 60_000;
    91→
    92→  // 1. Navigate to login page
    93→  await page.goto('/');
    94→
    95→  // 2. Wait for Core Kit to initialize (wallet button becomes enabled)
    96→  const walletButton = page.locator('[data-testid="wallet-login-button"]');
    97→  await walletButton.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
    98→  // Poll until the button is enabled (Core Kit init can take several seconds)
    99→  await page.waitForFunction(
   100→    () => {
   101→      const btn = document.querySelector('[data-testid="wallet-login-button"]') as HTMLButtonElement;
   102→      return btn && !btn.disabled;
   103→    },
   104→    { timeout: 20_000 }
   105→  );
   106→
   107→  // 3. Click wallet button to show connector list
   108→  await walletButton.click();
   109→
   110→  // 4. Select Mock Wallet from the connector list
   111→  const connectorList = page.locator('.wallet-connector-list');
   112→  await connectorList.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 5_000 });
   113→  const mockWalletOption = page.locator('.wallet-connector-option', { hasText: 'Mock Wallet' });
   114→  await mockWalletOption.click();
   115→
   116→  // 5. Wait for outcome: either /files redirect or DeviceWaitingScreen
   117→  const result = await Promise.race([
   118→    page
   119→      .waitForURL('**/files', { timeout })
   120→      .then(() => ({ outcome: 'success' as const })),
   121→    page
   122→      .locator('[data-testid="device-waiting"]')
   123→      .waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout })
   124→      .then(() => ({ outcome: 'requiredShare' as const })),
   125→  ]);
   126→
   127→  return result;
   128→}

    14→import { useMfaStore } from '../stores/mfa.store';
    15→import { getOrCreateDeviceIdentity } from '../lib/device/identity';
    16→import { detectDeviceInfo } from '../lib/device/info';
    17→
    18→export type FactorInfo = {
    19→  factorPubHex: string;
    20→  description: string;
    21→  type: string;
    22→  /** Additional metadata set during createFactor (e.g. deviceId, browserName) */
    23→  additionalMetadata?: Record<string, string>;
    24→};
    25→
    26→export function useMfa() {
    27→  const { coreKit } = useCoreKit();
    28→
    29→  const isMfaEnabled = useMfaStore((s) => s.isMfaEnabled);
    30→  const isEnrolling = useMfaStore((s) => s.isEnrolling);
    31→  const factorCount = useMfaStore((s) => s.factorCount);
    32→  const threshold = useMfaStore((s) => s.threshold);
    33→
    34→  /**
    35→   * Check MFA status from Core Kit key details.
    36→   * MFA is enabled when totalFactors > 2 (every account starts with 2
    37→   * default factors: JWT verifier share + hashedShare cloud custodial key).
    38→   */
    39→  const checkMfaStatus = useCallback((): {
    40→    isMfaEnabled: boolean;
    41→    totalFactors: number;
    42→    threshold: number;
    43→  } => {
    44→    if (!coreKit || coreKit.status !== COREKIT_STATUS.LOGGED_IN) {
    45→      return { isMfaEnabled: false, totalFactors: 0, threshold: 0 };
    46→    }
    47→    try {
    48→      const details = coreKit.getKeyDetails();
    49→      const enabled = details.totalFactors > 2;
    50→      useMfaStore.getState().setMfaEnabled(enabled);
    51→      useMfaStore.getState().setFactorDetails(details.totalFactors, details.threshold);
    52→      return {
    53→        isMfaEnabled: enabled,
    54→        totalFactors: details.totalFactors,
    55→        threshold: details.threshold,
    56→      };
    57→    } catch {
    58→      return { isMfaEnabled: false, totalFactors: 0, threshold: 0 };
    59→    }
    60→  }, [coreKit]);
    61→
    62→  /**
    63→   * Enable MFA. Returns 24-word recovery mnemonic.
    64→   * CRITICAL: commitChanges() must be called before enableMFA() in manualSync mode.
    65→   */
    66→  const enableMfa = useCallback(async (): Promise<string> => {
    67→    if (!coreKit) throw new Error('Core Kit not initialized');
    68→    if (coreKit.status !== COREKIT_STATUS.LOGGED_IN) {
    69→      throw new Error('Must be logged in to enable MFA');
    70→    }
    71→
    72→    const store = useMfaStore.getState();
    73→    if (store.isMfaEnabled) {
    74→      throw new Error('MFA is already enabled');
    75→    }
    76→
    77→    useMfaStore.getState().setEnrolling(true);
    78→    try {
    79→      // Commit any pending changes first (CRITICAL for manualSync mode -- Pitfall 1)
    80→      await coreKit.commitChanges();
    81→
    82→      // Capture TSS public key BEFORE enableMFA for stability verification (MFA-04)
    83→      const preMfaTssPub = coreKit.getKeyDetails().tssPubKey;
    84→
    85→      // enableMFA creates device factor + recovery factor atomically
    86→      const backupFactorKeyHex = await coreKit.enableMFA({
    87→        shareDescription: FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.SeedPhrase,
    88→      });
    89→
    90→      // Commit the MFA changes
    91→      await coreKit.commitChanges();
    92→
    93→      // Defensive check: verify TSS public key unchanged after MFA enrollment (MFA-04)
    94→      const postMfaTssPub = coreKit.getKeyDetails().tssPubKey;
    95→      if (preMfaTssPub?.x && preMfaTssPub?.y && postMfaTssPub?.x && postMfaTssPub?.y) {
    96→        const preX = preMfaTssPub.x.toString('hex');
    97→        const preY = preMfaTssPub.y.toString('hex');
    98→        const postX = postMfaTssPub.x.toString('hex');
    99→        const postY = postMfaTssPub.y.toString('hex');
   100→        if (preX !== postX || preY !== postY) {
   101→          throw new Error(
   102→            'MFA enrollment failed: TSS public key changed. Your keypair identity is no longer stable. Please contact support.'
   103→          );
   104→        }
   105→      }
   106→
   107→      // Convert to 24-word mnemonic for user display
   108→      const mnemonic = keyToMnemonic(backupFactorKeyHex);
   109→
   110→      // Update store with new key details
   111→      const details = coreKit.getKeyDetails();
   112→      useMfaStore.getState().setMfaEnabled(true);
   113→      useMfaStore.getState().setFactorDetails(details.totalFactors, details.threshold);
   114→
   115→      return mnemonic;
   116→    } finally {
   117→      useMfaStore.getState().setEnrolling(false);
   118→    }
   119→  }, [coreKit]);
   120→
   121→  /**
   122→   * Input a factor key (hex string) to complete REQUIRED_SHARE login.
   123→   * Used for both recovery and cross-device approval flows.
   124→   *
   125→   * IMPORTANT: Does NOT call syncStatus() because doing so would transition
   126→   * Core Kit's React context to LOGGED_IN, which triggers the session
   127→   * restoration effect in useAuth.ts. Since backend auth hasn't completed yet
   128→   * (no valid access token or refresh cookie), the session restore fails and
   129→   * calls coreKitLogout(), effectively undoing the recovery.
   130→   *
   131→   * The caller (completeRequiredShare) is responsible for syncing status
   132→   * AFTER backend auth completes.
   133→   */
   134→  const inputFactorKey = useCallback(
   135→    async (factorKeyHex: string): Promise<void> => {
   136→      if (!coreKit) throw new Error('Core Kit not initialized');
   137→      const factorKey = new BN(factorKeyHex, 'hex');
   138→      await coreKit.inputFactorKey(factorKey);
   139→      // syncStatus() deliberately omitted — see comment above
   140→    },
   141→    [coreKit]
   142→  );
   143→
   144→  /**
   145→   * Recover with a 24-word mnemonic phrase.
   146→   * After recovery, creates a device factor for the new device.
   147→   */
   148→  const recoverWithMnemonic = useCallback(
   149→    async (mnemonic: string): Promise<void> => {
   150→      if (!coreKit) throw new Error('Core Kit not initialized');
   151→
   152→      // Convert mnemonic to factor key hex
   153→      const factorKeyHex = mnemonicToKey(mnemonic.trim().toLowerCase());
   154→      await inputFactorKey(factorKeyHex);
   155→
   156→      // Create a device factor for this new device with metadata
   157→      const newDeviceFactor = generateFactorKey();
   158→      const deviceKeypair = await getOrCreateDeviceIdentity();
   159→      const deviceInfo = detectDeviceInfo();
   160→      await coreKit.createFactor({
   161→        shareType: TssShareType.DEVICE,
   162→        factorKey: newDeviceFactor.private,
   163→        shareDescription: FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.DeviceShare,
   164→        additionalMetadata: {
   165→          deviceId: deviceKeypair.deviceId,
   166→          browserName: deviceInfo.name,
   167→        },
   168→      });
   169→      await coreKit.setDeviceFactor(newDeviceFactor.private);
   170→      await coreKit.commitChanges();
   171→    },
   172→    [coreKit, inputFactorKey]
   173→  );
   174→
   175→  /**
   176→   * Get all factors with their descriptions.
   177→   * shareDescriptions is Record<string, string[]> where keys are factor pub hex.
   178→   */
   179→  const getFactors = useCallback((): FactorInfo[] => {
   180→    if (!coreKit || coreKit.status !== COREKIT_STATUS.LOGGED_IN) return [];
   181→    try {
   182→      const details = coreKit.getKeyDetails();
   183→      const factors: FactorInfo[] = [];
   184→
   185→      // Known system fields stored by Web3Auth in the flat JSON description.
   186→      // Everything else is user-provided additionalMetadata (spread at top level by addFactorDescription).
   187→      const systemFields = new Set(['module', 'dateAdded', 'tssShareIndex', 'tssIndex']);
   188→
   189→      for (const [factorPubHex, descriptions] of Object.entries(details.shareDescriptions)) {
   190→        for (const descJson of descriptions) {
   191→          try {
   192→            const parsed = JSON.parse(descJson) as Record<string, unknown>;
   193→            const module = (parsed.module as string) || 'unknown';
   194→            const tssShareIndex = parsed.tssShareIndex as number | undefined;
   195→
   196→            // Normalize type: enableMFA() creates factors with module="Other"
   197→            // but tssShareIndex correctly identifies 2=DEVICE, 3=RECOVERY
   198→            let type = module;
   199→            if (module === FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.Other || module === 'Other') {
   200→              if (tssShareIndex === 2) {
   201→                type = FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.DeviceShare;
   202→              } else if (tssShareIndex === 3) {
   203→                type = FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.SeedPhrase;
   204→              }
   205→            }
   206→
   207→            // Extract additionalMetadata from flat JSON (Web3Auth spreads it at top level)
   208→            const additionalMetadata: Record<string, string> = {};
   209→            for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(parsed)) {
   210→              if (!systemFields.has(key) && typeof value === 'string') {
   211→                additionalMetadata[key] = value;
   212→              }
   213→            }
   214→
   215→            factors.push({
   216→              factorPubHex,
   217→              description: type,
   218→              type,
   219→              additionalMetadata:
   220→                Object.keys(additionalMetadata).length > 0 ? additionalMetadata : undefined,
   221→            });
   222→          } catch {
   223→            factors.push({
   224→              factorPubHex,
   225→              description: 'unknown',
   226→              type: 'unknown',
   227→            });
   228→          }
   229→        }
   230→      }
   231→
   232→      return factors;
   233→    } catch {
   234→      return [];
   235→    }
   236→  }, [coreKit]);
   237→
   238→  /**
   239→   * Delete a factor by its public key hex.
   240→   * Cannot delete the currently active factor or the last remaining factor.
   241→   */
   242→  const deleteFactor = useCallback(
   243→    async (factorPubHex: string): Promise<void> => {
   244→      if (!coreKit) throw new Error('Core Kit not initialized');
   245→      const factorPub = Point.fromSEC1(factorKeyCurve, factorPubHex);
   246→      await coreKit.deleteFactor(factorPub);
   247→      await coreKit.commitChanges();
   248→    },
   249→    [coreKit]
   250→  );
   251→
   252→  /**
   253→   * Get the current active factor key and share type.
   254→   */
   255→  const getCurrentFactorKey = useCallback((): {
   256→    factorKey: BN;
   257→    shareType: TssShareType;
   258→  } | null => {
   259→    if (!coreKit || coreKit.status !== COREKIT_STATUS.LOGGED_IN) return null;
   260→    try {
   261→      return coreKit.getCurrentFactorKey();
   262→    } catch {
   263→      return null;
   264→    }
   265→  }, [coreKit]);
   266→
   267→  /**
   268→   * Regenerate the recovery phrase.
   269→   * Deletes the old recovery factor and creates a new one.
   270→   * Returns the new 24-word mnemonic.
   271→   */
   272→  const regenerateRecoveryPhrase = useCallback(async (): Promise<string> => {
   273→    if (!coreKit) throw new Error('Core Kit not initialized');
   274→    if (coreKit.status !== COREKIT_STATUS.LOGGED_IN) {
   275→      throw new Error('Must be logged in to regenerate recovery phrase');
   276→    }
   277→
   278→    // Find the existing recovery (seedPhrase) factor
   279→    const factors = getFactors();
   280→    const recoveryFactor = factors.find((f) => f.type === FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.SeedPhrase);
   281→
   282→    if (recoveryFactor) {
   283→      // Delete old recovery factor
   284→      const factorPub = Point.fromSEC1(factorKeyCurve, recoveryFactor.factorPubHex);
   285→      await coreKit.deleteFactor(factorPub);
   286→    }
   287→
   288→    // Generate new recovery factor
   289→    const newRecovery = generateFactorKey();
   290→    await coreKit.createFactor({
   291→      shareType: TssShareType.RECOVERY,
   292→      factorKey: newRecovery.private,
   293→      shareDescription: FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.SeedPhrase,
   294→    });
   295→    await coreKit.commitChanges();
   296→
   297→    // Convert the new factor key to mnemonic
   298→    // Zero-pad to 64 hex chars (32 bytes)
   299→    const factorKeyHex = newRecovery.private.toString('hex').padStart(64, '0');
   300→    return keyToMnemonic(factorKeyHex);
   301→  }, [coreKit, getFactors]);
   302→
   303→  return {
   304→    // State from store
   305→    isMfaEnabled,
   306→    isEnrolling,
   307→    factorCount,
   308→    threshold,
   309→
   310→    // Operations
   311→    checkMfaStatus,
   312→    enableMfa,
   313→    inputFactorKey,
   314→    recoverWithMnemonic,
   315→    getFactors,
   316→    deleteFactor,
   317→    getCurrentFactorKey,
   318→    regenerateRecoveryPhrase,
   319→  };
   320→}

    10→import { getCoreKit, initCoreKit, COREKIT_STATUS } from './core-kit';
    11→import type { Web3AuthMPCCoreKit } from './core-kit';
    12→
    13→interface CoreKitContextValue {
    14→  /** The Core Kit singleton instance (null until first render) */
    15→  coreKit: Web3AuthMPCCoreKit | null;
    16→  /** Current SDK status from the COREKIT_STATUS state machine */
    17→  status: COREKIT_STATUS;
    18→  /** True when status is anything other than NOT_INITIALIZED */
    19→  isInitialized: boolean;
    20→  /** True when status is LOGGED_IN (user fully authenticated) */
    21→  isLoggedIn: boolean;
    22→  /** True when status is REQUIRED_SHARE (MFA challenge needed -- Phase 12.4) */
    23→  isRequiredShare: boolean;
    24→  /** Initialization error, if any */
    25→  error: Error | null;
    26→  /** Re-run initialization (e.g., retry after error) */
    27→  reinitialize: () => Promise<void>;
    28→  /** Sync React state with CoreKit's internal status after login/logout/MFA */
    29→  syncStatus: () => void;
    30→}
    31→
    32→const CoreKitContext = createContext<CoreKitContextValue | null>(null);
    33→
    34→/**
    35→ * React context provider for MPC Core Kit.
    36→ *
    37→ * Initializes Core Kit on mount (calls init() which checks for existing sessions).
    38→ * Exposes the singleton instance and COREKIT_STATUS to child components.
    39→ * Mounted at the top of the component tree in main.tsx.
    40→ */
    41→export function CoreKitProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
    42→  const [status, setStatus] = useState<COREKIT_STATUS>(COREKIT_STATUS.NOT_INITIALIZED);
    43→  const [coreKit, setCoreKit] = useState<Web3AuthMPCCoreKit | null>(null);
    44→  const [error, setError] = useState<Error | null>(null);
    45→
    46→  const initialize = useCallback(async () => {
    47→    try {
    48→      setError(null);
    49→      const ck = getCoreKit();
    50→      setCoreKit(ck);
    51→      const resultStatus = await initCoreKit();
    52→      setStatus(resultStatus);
    53→    } catch (err) {
    54→      console.error('[CoreKit] Initialization failed:', err);
    55→      setError(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)));
    56→    }
    57→  }, []);
    58→
    59→  useEffect(() => {
    60→    initialize();
    61→  }, [initialize]);
    62→
    63→  /** Sync React state with CoreKit's internal status. Call after login/logout/MFA. */
    64→  const syncStatus = useCallback(() => {
    65→    const ck = getCoreKit();
    66→    setStatus(ck.status);
    67→  }, []);
    68→
    69→  const value: CoreKitContextValue = useMemo(
    70→    () => ({
    71→      coreKit,
    72→      status,
    73→      isInitialized: status !== COREKIT_STATUS.NOT_INITIALIZED,
    74→      isLoggedIn: status === COREKIT_STATUS.LOGGED_IN,
    75→      isRequiredShare: status === COREKIT_STATUS.REQUIRED_SHARE,
    76→      error,
    77→      reinitialize: initialize,
    78→      syncStatus,
    79→    }),
    80→    [coreKit, status, error, initialize, syncStatus]
    81→  );
    82→
    83→  return <CoreKitContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CoreKitContext.Provider>;
    84→}
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * Hook to access Core Kit instance and status from React components.
    88→ * Must be used within a CoreKitProvider.
    89→ */
    90→export function useCoreKit(): CoreKitContextValue {
    91→  const context = useContext(CoreKitContext);
    92→  if (!context) {
    93→    throw new Error('useCoreKit must be used within CoreKitProvider');
    94→  }
    95→  return context;
    96→}
    97→

     6→
     7→// Shared refresh promise eliminates race condition where multiple concurrent
     8→// 401 responses each trigger their own POST /auth/refresh before the boolean
     9→// flag could be set. The promise is assigned synchronously before any await,
    10→// so all concurrent 401 handlers see it immediately and share the same refresh.
    11→let refreshPromise: Promise<string> | null = null;
    12→
    13→export const apiClient = axios.create({
    14→  baseURL: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || 'http://localhost:3000',
    15→  withCredentials: true, // For HTTP-only refresh token cookie
    16→});
    17→
    18→// Request interceptor: Add access token to headers
    19→apiClient.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
    20→  const accessToken = useAuthStore.getState().accessToken;
    21→  if (accessToken) {
    22→    config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
    23→  }
    24→  return config;
    25→});
    26→
    27→// Response interceptor: Handle 401 and token refresh
    28→apiClient.interceptors.response.use(
    29→  (response) => response,
    30→  async (error) => {
    31→    const originalRequest = error.config;
    32→
    33→    // Don't retry refresh endpoint to avoid infinite loop
    34→    const isRefreshRequest = originalRequest?.url?.includes('/auth/refresh');
    35→
    36→    // Only handle 401 errors, and only retry once (but never retry refresh endpoint)
    37→    if (error.response?.status === 401 && !originalRequest._retry && !isRefreshRequest) {
    38→      originalRequest._retry = true;
    39→
    40→      // If a refresh is already in flight, all concurrent 401 handlers
    41→      // await the same promise instead of firing duplicate refresh requests.
    42→      if (refreshPromise) {
    43→        const token = await refreshPromise;
    44→        originalRequest.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
    45→        return apiClient(originalRequest);
    46→      }
    47→
    48→      // First 401 handler: create the refresh promise synchronously (before any await)
    49→      // so subsequent 401 handlers in the same microtask see it immediately.
    50→      refreshPromise = apiClient
    51→        .post<{ accessToken: string }>('/auth/refresh')
    52→        .then((response) => {
    53→          const { accessToken } = response.data;
    54→          useAuthStore.getState().setAccessToken(accessToken);
    55→          return accessToken;
    56→        })
    57→        .catch((refreshError) => {
    58→          // [SECURITY: HIGH-03] Clear all stores including crypto keys on token refresh failure
    59→          useFolderStore.getState().clearFolders();
    60→          useVaultStore.getState().clearVaultKeys();

    62→          useAuthStore.getState().logout();
    63→          // Redirect to login will be handled by route guard
    64→          throw refreshError;
    65→        })
    66→        .finally(() => {
    67→          refreshPromise = null;
    68→        });
    69→
    70→      const token = await refreshPromise;
    71→      originalRequest.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
    72→      return apiClient(originalRequest);
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    throw error;
    76→  }

   173→function CountdownValue({ expiresAt }: { expiresAt: number }) {

   180→    }, 1000);
   181→    return () => {
   182→      if (intervalRef.current) clearInterval(intervalRef.current);
   183→    };
   184→  }, [expiresAt]);
   185→
   186→  const minutes = Math.floor(remaining / 60000);
   187→  const seconds = Math.floor((remaining % 60000) / 1000);
   188→  const isWarning = remaining <= 3 * 60 * 1000 && remaining > 0;
   189→
   190→  return (
   191→    <span
   192→      className={`device-approval-detail-value device-approval-countdown ${isWarning ? 'warning' : ''}`}
   193→    >
   194→      {remaining > 0 ? `${minutes}:${seconds.toString().padStart(2, '0')}` : 'expired'}
   195→    </span>
   196→  );
   197→}

   199→/**
   200→ * Format a timestamp as a relative time string (e.g. "just now", "2m ago").

   202→function formatTimeAgo(timestampMs: number): string {
   203→  const diff = Date.now() - timestampMs;
   204→  if (diff < 60_000) return 'just now';
   205→  if (diff < 3_600_000) return `${Math.floor(diff / 60_000)}m ago`;
   206→  return `${Math.floor(diff / 3_600_000)}h ago`;

> AGENT

Now I can see the exact issue. The nav trap confirms:
- **1 navigation captured**: pushState to `#/files` from `#/settings`
- Stack trace: `handleSiweFlow → Login.tsx → useAuth.ts:247`

The root cause is a **race between two navigate('/files') calls**:

1. **Early navigate** (from Login.tsx redirect effect): When `completeBackendAuth` calls `setAccessToken()`, `isAuthenticated` becomes true, triggering Login.tsx's `useEffect(() => { if (isAuthenticated) navigate('/files') })`. This fires BEFORE `initializeOrLoadVault()` completes. The test's `waitForURL('**/files')` resolves here.

2. **Late navigate** (from loginWithWallet): After `initializeOrLoadVault()` finally completes, `completeBackendAuth` returns, and `loginWithWallet` calls its explicit `navigate('/files')`. But by now the user has navigated to `/settings` for MFA enrollment.

The fix: remove the redundant `navigate('/files')` from the login functions — the Login.tsx redirect effect already handles it.

## Summary

I've conducted a thorough search and found all device approval related code in the CipherBox web app. Here are the complete file paths and a detailed breakdown:

### Core Hook Implementation
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/hooks/useDeviceApproval.ts`

This is the main hook managing both sides of the cross-device approval flow:
- **Requester (new device):** Generates ephemeral secp256k1 keypair, creates bulletin board request, polls for approval status
- **Approver (existing device):** Polls for pending requests, ECIES-encrypts factor key for approval
- Manages 11 functions/actions:
  - `requestApproval()` - Create approval request
  - `cancelRequest()` - Cancel pending request
  - `approveRequest()` - Approve with encrypted factor key
  - `denyRequest()` - Deny request
  - `pollPendingRequests()` - Start polling for pending requests
  - `stopApproverPolling()` - Stop polling
  - Plus state management: `approvalStatus`, `approvalError`, `pendingRequests`

### Device Approval Service (API Client Wrapper)
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/services/device-approval.service.ts`

Thin wrapper around generated Orval client with 5 main methods:
- `createRequest()` - POST `/device-approval/request`
- `getStatus()` - GET `/device-approval/{requestId}/status`
- `getPending()` - GET `/device-approval/pending`
- `respond()` - POST `/device-approval/{requestId}/respond`
- `cancel()` - DELETE `/device-approval/{requestId}`

### Generated API Client
**File:** `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/api/device-approval/device-approval.ts`

Auto-generated by Orval from OpenAPI spec. Exports:
- Raw endpoint functions: `deviceApprovalControllerCreateRequest`, `deviceApprovalControllerGetStatus`, etc.
- React Query hooks: `useDeviceApprovalControllerCreateRequest`, `useDeviceApprovalControllerGetStatus`, etc.

### Components Using Device Approval

**1. DeviceApprovalModal** (`/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/components/mfa/DeviceApprovalModal.tsx`)
- Displays overlay on existing (already logged-in) device
- Shows pending approval requests with device name, creation time, countdown timer
- Approve/Deny buttons with error handling
- Queues requests (shows one at a time)
- Mounted in AppShell

**2. DeviceWaitingScreen** (`/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/web/src/components/mfa/DeviceWaitingScreen.tsx`)
- Full-screen waiting component on new device in REQUIRED_SHARE state
- Manages countdown (5 minutes TTL)
- Displays approval states: pending, denied, expired, error, completing
- Fallback link to use recovery phrase instead
